## A note on requirement identity — a documented deviation from the agent specification

The agent specification says to extract requirements as `REQ-001`, `REQ-002` and so on. **That has not
been done, deliberately.** The sources already carry a numbered register of **424 defined `FR-###`
rows** whose ids are cited by the schema, the API contract, the backlog, the test-case register and the
traceability appendix, and the repository rule is explicit: *"Register ids are never renumbered."*
Minting a parallel `REQ-###` space over it would create exactly the traceability breakage that rule
exists to prevent, and would silently orphan every downstream citation.

**`FR-###` is therefore the requirement identity throughout this report.** Findings raised *by this
analysis* — which have no existing id — are numbered in this document's own spaces: `RA-G##` (gaps),
`RA-AMB##` (ambiguities), `RA-CON##` (contradictions), `RA-MS##` (missing scenarios), `RA-ASM##`
(assumptions), `RA-AC##` (proposed acceptance criteria), `RA-Q##` (clarification questions) and
`RA-R##` (risks). Where a finding restates an existing `G##`, `OI-##` or `Q##`, that id is carried and
**no new number is minted**.

---

## 1. Executive Summary

### 1.1 Purpose

The Flat Wire Mill module is the **shopfloor and dashboard layer** for three new Flattening Lines — FL1,
FL2 and the hybrid FL3 — that convert aluminium rod into coreless oscillated flat wire coils. It is a
new capability *inside* the existing UAL Manufacturing Execution System, not a standalone application
[`[REQ §1.2]`, `[MS §1.1]`].

### 1.2 Business objective

*(Explicit information — `[MS §1.2]`.)*

1. **Lower unit cost than pancake (strip) coils**, opening a new market — notably welding-wire buyers.
2. **Weld genealogy as a contractual deliverable.** Welding-wire customers require a traceable chain
   from supplier heat, through every rod-to-rod induction weld, to the finished coil alpha, with
   footage attribution per source rod (`NFR012`).
3. Existing UAL applications cannot represent rod as an input, a flattening operation, a bundle width,
   an edge type or a coreless oscillated coil — roughly **24 applications** need extension.

### 1.3 Scope

**In scope** *(explicit — `[MS §1.3]`)*: the operator screens (pre-check-in, check-in for rod and spool,
active-run monitoring, welding, SPC, roll adjust, die change, pause/resume, WIP rejection, rod checkout,
coil completion, packing); the dashboards (Line Status DB1, Active Run DB3, Pass Schedule DB9/DB9A,
Shift Summary DB10, Roll Adjust DB11, Rod Checkout DB12, Die Change, Die Management, OEE); the
standalone **`FlatWireDB`** schema and the named legacy integration points; PLC tag push/clear, OPC tag
consumption and SignalR streaming; and SPC checkpoints, SPC-HOLD, CPK and WIP rejection.

**Known out of scope** *(explicit — `[TS §2.2]`, `[REQ §2.1]`)*: rod receiving (`R#####` generation,
chemistry, weight validation); order planning and line scheduling; the Web changes (Orders, Quotes,
IQR, Item Template, Vendor); Coil Yield and Cost Ledger internals; OPC server behaviour.

**Withdrawn from scope by client decision, 4 Aug 2026:** Dashboard 13 (HMI Line Schematic, `FR-440`–
`FR-451`), Dashboard 14 (SCADA Trends, `FR-460`–`FR-470`), and the Active Run Machine View tab
(`FR-111`, `FR-112`, `FR-114`, `FR-425`).

**Deferred to MVP-2:** Die Management (§5.10), Pass Schedule Management DB9 (§5.18), Pass Schedule List
DB9A (§5.19), Shift Summary DB10 (§5.23), OEE Dashboard (§5.24). ⚠ **This is a scope contradiction, not
a clean deferral** — see `RA-CON01`.

### 1.4 Overall assessment

The register is **unusually mature in coverage and unusually fragile in consistency.** Its strengths are
real and should be said plainly: requirements are grouped by operator workflow with actors,
preconditions, field-level validation, state changes, error paths and real-time events stated per group;
non-functional constraints are folded *inline* into the functional group they constrain rather than
annexed; open issues are registered rather than papered over; and superseded text is retained in place
rather than deleted, so a reader can see what changed and why.

Against that, four structural problems make the register **not yet safe to build the whole of**:

1. **The register does not agree with itself on how many requirements it holds.** Three different
   totals are asserted — 279, 395 and a measured 424 (`RA-CON02`).
2. **A large fraction of the register is `[PROPOSED]` — written by the delivery team, never
   client-reviewed.** Sections §5.25, §5.26, §5.27, §5.28, §5.29 and §5.30 are `[PROPOSED]` in whole or
   near-whole: that is **69 requirements**, roughly **16 % of the register**, carrying `Must` priority
   and feeding the schema, the shared-database write-back and the welding-wire certificate.
3. **Client answers received on 9 September 2026 contradict requirements that are still written the
   old way, and nothing has been edited.** `Q19` (FL2 gauge tracking) and `Q22` (rod tolerance grain)
   are both live contradictions today — `G120` and `G121`, `RA-CON03` and `RA-CON04`.
4. **Authorisation is specified in six columns and implemented in none.** `D-52` (6 Sep 2026) makes the
   whole role matrix an MVP-2 obligation, while ~20 requirements across the register state role
   restrictions as functional behaviour (`RA-CON05`).

| **CF-2** | **`FR-153`'s ±2 % weight-variance threshold is arithmetically unreachable from target dimensions.** Gauge ±0.002 on 0.110 (±1.8 %) stacked with width ±0.005 on 0.625 (±0.8 %) is ±2.6 % worst case on fully conforming material | `[REQ §5.5]`, stated in the source | The supervisor override fires on good material. Specified behaviour is self-defeating |

This is the highest-traffic screen in the module |

### 1.6 Readiness

> ## 🔴 **NOT READY**
>
> Assessed against the agent's own bar: *"Do not mark READY when unresolved critical ambiguity,
> contradiction, missing business rule, or other material uncertainty could change implementation or
> testing."*
>
> The register is **READY WITH MINOR CLARIFICATIONS for roughly two-thirds of its surface** — the
> operator screens whose behaviour is stated, mocked and constrained (pre-check-in, check-in wizard
> steps, active run monitor, pause/resume, roll adjust, die change, WIP rejection, rod checkout modes).
>
> It is **NOT READY** as a whole, for four independent reasons, any one of which is sufficient:
>
> 1. **Ten Critical open issues remain** — `OI-01`, `OI-39`, `OI-45`, `OI-46`, `OI-47`, `OI-48`,
>    `OI-49`, `OI-50`, `OI-51`, plus `G54` and `G40` at Critical severity in the gap register.
> 2. **69 `Must` requirements are `[PROPOSED]` and never client-reviewed**, and they carry the
>    shared-database write-back and the certificate genealogy.
> 3. **Four requirements are known-unimplementable as written** — `FR-280`–`FR-282` (no host),
>    `FR-297` (no column), `FR-563` (blocked on `Q87`), `FR-175` (no host).
> 4. **Two client answers dated 9 September 2026 contradict the standing text and have not been
>    propagated** (`G120`, `G121`).
>
> **`BLOCKED` was considered and rejected.** Work is not stopped: the phases whose requirements are
> settled can proceed. The blockage is per-phase, and §13's traceability matrix says which.

ranges — and `FR-512` is deleted. Method: `grep -oE '^\| ~?~?\*\*FR-[0-9]{3}[a-z]?\*\*'` over both files,

`S` security/authorisation · `A` audit/logging · `N` notification · `R` reporting · `NFR` non-functional.
**Status key:** `Live` · `Proposed` (`[PROPOSED]`, never client-reviewed) · `Superseded` ·
`Withdrawn` · `Deleted` · `Blocked` (cannot be built as written).

| FR-565 | A part identity is **opaque** — never parsed, rebuilt, or used for ordering; ordering comes from the footage range | BR | `[ORD020]` | Must | Proposed |
| FR-566 | A single-source coil has **exactly one** part identity equal to its scalar reference and writes **exactly one** shared record | BR | `[PROPOSED]` | Must | Proposed |
| FR-567 | Part weights are **apportioned, never repeated**; the sum equals the coil's net weight; skid totals accumulate **once per physical coil** | BR | `Q89` | Must | Proposed |
| FR-568 | Each part's genealogy record names **its own** source rod. ⚠ **A shared primary rod across all parts is not acceptable** | D,BR | `Q89` | Must | Proposed — the condition on which `OI-113` closes |
| FR-569 | The retry contract is the **set** of part identities already written, recorded per part as it commits; a retry writes only the unrecorded parts and reports **all** of them | BR,I | supersedes `FR-518` | Must | Proposed |
| FR-570 | The two-coils-per-skid rule is expressed and enforced in **physical coils**, not shared coil records. ⚠ **Amends `FR-335`, which is `[CONFIRMED]` — requires client re-sign-off** | BR | amends `FR-335`, `PKG003` | Must | **Proposed — re-sign-off owed** |

## 3. Detailed Requirement Analysis

Ten clusters are analysed in depth. Selection criterion: a cluster is analysed here if it is **on the
critical path**, **contractual**, **cross-system**, or **carries an unresolved Critical issue**. Clusters
not analysed individually are covered by the inventory (§2), the gap and ambiguity registers (§4–§6) and
the traceability matrix (§13).

---

### DRA-1 · Pass-schedule acknowledgement and the PLC tag push — `FR-070`–`FR-075`, `FR-049`, `FR-391`

**Original wording (key excerpts).** `FR-070`: *"retrieve the applicable pass schedule at check-in via
**attribute lookup** (alloy + rod diameter + target gauge × width + route mode), surface the
recommendation in a **confirm bar**…"* · `FR-073`: *"push component activation flags, die sizes, roll
gaps, speed limits and gauge/width targets to the controller for the selected payoff position, **as one
batch**"* · `FR-074`: *"If any individual tag write fails, an exception shall be raised, **compensating
writes shall re-clear the tags already written** and revert the shared-schema changes, and the check-in
shall be aborted."*

**Interpretation.** This is the single path by which the physical machine is configured. Nothing else in
the system writes machine configuration: `FR-049` bans a PLC write at pre-check-in and `FR-391` bans one
during schedule generation. The pass schedule is data; **the operator's acknowledgement is the act.**

| Aspect | Content |
|---|---|
| **Type** | Functional · business rule · integration · audit |
| **Actors** | FL1/FL2/FL3 operator (acknowledges); Supervisor (inspection override, `FR-081`); the system (writes) |
| **Preconditions** | Rod `STAGED` or scanned directly · an **`Active`** pass schedule exists for the attribute combination · the job is scheduled · the real-time backbone is up · wizard steps 1–6 cleared or an override is on file (`FR-079`) |
| **Trigger** | Operator presses **Acknowledge & Begin Check-in** |
| **Inputs** | Rod alpha, measured diameter (M1/M2 → ovality), scrap box (optional), payoff position, selected schedule id, deviation reason where the recommendation is not taken |
| **Outputs** | `FlatWireRun` (`Status='Running'`, `StartedAt`) · `RodCheckin` · `SpcCheckpoint(PreRun)` + measurements · `RodStaging → CheckedIn` · `Rod.Status='INFLAT'` · PLC tag batch · `LineStatus{Running}`, `PayoffStateChanged{Active}`, `ComponentStatus` |
| **Business rules** | Records **before** the push, always (`FR-072`) · one batch per acknowledgement (`FR-073`) · FL3 pushes **all FM1 and FM2 tags in one batch** and creates **no `SpoolProcessing` row** (`FR-083`) · a non-recommended schedule requires a free-text reason and is flagged for Operations review (`FR-071`) |
| **Validations** | Order open · plan open · mandatory fields complete · diameter inside the min/max band · rod available (`FR-067`) · schedule is not `Draft` (→ `422`) · no active run on the line (→ `409`) |
| **Main flow** | Lookup → recommend → confirm bar → operator acknowledges → **audit + run records written** → PLC batch pushed → outcome recorded in `PlcTagsPushed` → per-write audit → operator returned to **DB2A** (`FR-079a`) |
| **Alternative flows** | Operator selects a non-recommended schedule → reason captured, flagged · inspection step failed → supervisor override with badge, password and reason (`FR-081`) · rod arrived via pre-check-in → payoff selector pre-filled read-only (`FR-082`) |
| **Exception handling** | Any tag write fails → exception, **compensating re-clear** of already-written tags, revert shared-schema changes, abort (`FR-074`) · PLC push failed → `500`, check-in aborted · payoff mismatch against the staged row → `409` |
| **Dependencies** | `OPCConnection` (write surface) · `[PLC]` tag paths · the `CommonDB` `OPCTags` registration (`D-44`) · `united_db..alloys` · `planning_routings` · Phase 2 (Pass Schedule) — **the highest dependency in the project** |

**Issues — this cluster carries four, and two are blocking.**

1. ⛔ **`FR-074` cannot be implemented from the response.** `G58`: `OPCConnection.WriteTag` returns
   **`200` regardless of outcome** and reports no write failure to its caller. The requirement's entire
   trigger condition — *"if any individual tag write fails"* — is not observable through the interface
   it must observe it through. **This is a blocking defect in the integration contract, not in the
   requirement.**
2. ⛔ **`FR-070`'s no-match path is undefined** — `OI-46`, Critical. The specified behaviour covers
   *found* and *found-but-not-recommended*; **not found** has no path. The stub assumes a single active
   schedule.
3. ⚠ **`FR-073` may be specifying a write the client says never happens.** `Q27` (answered 9 Sep 2026)
   *deletes a PLC write — line speed is controlled at the HMI and never sent.* `FR-073` lists *"speed
   limits"* among the pushed values, and `PLC-Q06` records that "speed limits" versus "speed targets"
   is itself unresolved. The requirement is now **stale in the unsafe direction**: building it as
   written pushes a tag the controller does not accept.
4. ⚠ **`FR-083`'s single FL3 batch has no controller to be single against.** `G99`: FL3 has no
   controller of its own, so an FL3 push must write to **two** controllers — and nothing is built or
   specified for that. "One batch" is a requirement about atomicity across a boundary that turns out to
   be two boundaries.

**Acceptance criteria — extracted.** `FR-072` states the ordering obligation testably (*records before
push, recovery marker on write failure*). `FR-075` states the outcome-recording obligation testably.
**Proposed** criteria are at `RA-AC01`–`RA-AC04`.

---

### DRA-2 · The MMS ID lifecycle — `FR-013`, with `FR-009`, `FR-014`

**Original wording.** *"generate a unique **MMS ID per input coil at check-in**, activate it when a
welded coil becomes active, automatically close the previous one, and close MMS IDs **strictly on
material consumption** (remaining ft = 0) — **never on operator action**. An output spool may reference
multiple MMS IDs."*

**Interpretation.** The MMS ID is the material-management handle for one *input* coil's passage through
the line. Its lifecycle is deliberately **machine-driven, not operator-driven** — which is what makes it
safe for `FR-009` to use "no active MMS ID" as an ITInhibit set condition.

| Aspect | Content |
|---|---|
| **Type** | Data · business rule |
| **Actors** | The system only. **No actor may close an MMS ID** |
| **Trigger** | Open: check-in of an input coil. Activate: a welded coil becoming active. Close: remaining ft reaching 0 |
| **Business rules** | One MMS ID per input coil · activation on weld transition · automatic close of the previous · close **strictly on consumption** · **an output spool may reference many MMS IDs** (many-to-one, spool ← MMS) |
| **Dependencies** | PLC feet consumption (`FR-014`) · the weld transition (`FR-169`, driven **solely** by consumption reaching 0 ft) · ITInhibit (`FR-009`) |

**Issues.**

1. ⛔ **`OI-03` — the MMS ID has no defined format.** `[BR §3.3]` lists it in the alpha-format table with
   the value *"(no format defined)"*. Every other identifier in the system has one. **A `Must`
   requirement to *generate a unique* identifier does not say what it generates.**
2. ⚠ **Two independent statements both claim to drive the payoff transition, and they are the same
   statement said twice.** `FR-013` closes an MMS ID on remaining ft = 0; `FR-051` and `FR-169` drive
   the payoff transition on consumption reaching 0 ft. These are consistent, but nothing says whether
   the MMS close and the payoff transition are **one event or two**, or which is observable first.
   That matters for `FR-009`: if the close precedes the next open by any interval, **ITInhibit fires
   between two consecutive rods on a healthy line.** Raised as `RA-AMB03`.
3. ⚠ **No requirement states what happens to an open MMS ID on a Mode B mid-run checkout or on an
   aborted run.** The rod leaves the line with material unconsumed, so "close strictly on consumption"
   never fires. Raised as `RA-MS07`.

---

### DRA-3 · ITInhibit — `FR-008`, `FR-009`, `FR-010`, `FR-020`

**Original wording.** `FR-008`: *"**ITInhibit** as a system-controlled PLC tag that blocks machine run,
set and cleared **only** automatically — never by an operator."*

| Aspect | Content |
|---|---|
| **Type** | Business rule · integration · safety-adjacent |
| **Actors** | The system only — **explicitly no operator** |
| **Set conditions** | (1) no coil/rod checked in · (2) no active MMS ID · (3) PLC feet data unavailable or invalid · (4) two or more consecutive data recordings missing |
| **Effect** | Block machine run and related transactions; record no rolling data without an active coil (`FR-010`); display a prominent alert on condition (4) (`FR-020`) |
| **Dependencies** | MMS ID lifecycle · OPC feet tag · the recording cadence (`FR-018`) |

**Issues.**

1. ⛔ **`G80` — the client's eight IT inhibit reasons and `[PLC §8.2]`'s five set conditions share
   exactly one.** The overlap is *"no coil or rod is checked in"*. `FR-009` enumerates four (the source
   IDs run `ALT002`–`ALT005`); the specification carries five; the client carries eight. **Three
   different set-condition sets are live in the repository.** This is the highest-consequence
   contradiction in the cross-cutting group because ITInhibit is the interlock.
2. ⛔ **`G81` — `No Qualified Operators Are Logged In` presumes a mechanism that does not exist.** The
   client marks this reason as applying to flat wire. Nothing in the register defines operator
   *qualification*, and `FR-001`–`FR-005` cover punch-in status and per-run association, not
   qualification.
3. ⚠ **Line scoping is asserted in `[TS §2.3]` and nowhere in the register.** The test strategy requires
   *"that it is line-scoped — a blocked line must not block the other two"* (`[PLC §8.1]`, `D15`).
   **`FR-008`–`FR-010` never say this.** A developer building from `[REQ]` alone could reasonably
   implement a global inhibit. Raised as `RA-G03`.
4. ⚠ **Condition (4) is stated twice with different consequences.** `FR-009` sets ITInhibit on ≥2
   consecutive missing recordings; `FR-020` additionally requires a prominent alert. Neither says
   whether the alert is the DB1 alert panel (`FR-422`) or a screen-local banner, and the alert panel has
   no persistence (`OI-28`).

---

### DRA-4 · Footage → weight — `FR-137`, `FR-332`, `FR-332a`, `FR-015`, `FR-151`–`FR-153`, `FR-559`

**Original wording.** `FR-137`: *"`(current footage − footage at spool start) × lb-per-ft`, where
`lb-per-ft = A(in²) × 12 × ρ` — `A` applying the round-edge correction where applicable, and ρ read from
**`united_db..alloys.alloy_density`**."*

**Interpretation.** One formula, one density source, **one open variable — the dimensional basis.** Every
weight the system reports (spool milestone, spool completion, coil net weight, yield, cost, order
consumption, remaining-weight estimate) resolves through this.

| Aspect | Content |
|---|---|
| **Type** | Business rule · data · reporting |
| **Business rules** | Weight is **derived, never weighed during rolling** (`FR-015`, `FR-332`) · a scale reading may **override** at completion (`FR-151`, `FR-152`) · **both weights and the variance persist regardless of basis** (`FR-155`) · FL2 takes gauge and width **from the schedule / order, not live measurement** (`FR-137`) |
| **Worked reference (stated in source)** | 1100 at 0.110″ × 0.625″ → **0.0809 lb/ft** square edge, **0.0778** round edge. `spool_notification.js`'s `24,900 ft × 0.0809 = 2,014 lb` checks out |
| **Banned variant** | `FR-332a`: the mockup's `14,200 ft × 0.069 lb/ft` **shall not be implemented** — back-solving 0.069 implies ρ = 0.0836 lb/in³, which is not aluminium |

**Issues — this is the highest-value cluster in the register and it carries four.**

1. ⭐ **The open decision has just closed and the requirements do not say so.** `Q10`'s dimensional basis
   landed **9 September 2026: NOMINAL, with the round-edge correction at FL1 output.** `FR-332`,
   `FR-137`, `FR-559` and `OI-45` are all still written as undecided. **`OI-45` should close and has
   not.** This is `CF-1`.
2. ⛔ **`FR-153`'s ±2 % threshold is unreachable from target dimensions.** The source states the
   arithmetic itself: gauge ±0.002 on 0.110 is ±1.8 %; width ±0.005 on 0.625 is ±0.8 %; stacked, ±2.6 %
   on **fully conforming** material. The specified override therefore fires on good product. The source
   recommends deriving weight by **integrating over `RunReading`** — which the `Q10` answer (nominal)
   **does not do**, so the defect survives the decision. This is `CF-2`, and `FR-559` inherits it by
   citation.
3. ⚠ **`FR-137`'s FL2 clause rests on a premise the client has just contradicted.** *"For FL2, gauge and
   width shall come from the pass schedule / order, not live measurement, because FL2 broadcasts
   `null`"* — and `Q19` says FL2 tracks gauge and width throughout the run (`G120`). If `Q19` is taken
   at face value the *reason* in `FR-137` is void even if the *rule* is still wanted.
4. ⚠ **`Q93` — six readings in the client's own formula document cannot be settled from the page**, and
   one of them decides whether the nominal product is makeable: the two footage formulas use a
   **square-edge** area where the two area formulas use a **rounded** one.

**Acceptance criteria — extracted.** `FR-332a` is unusually good: it states a **negative** acceptance
criterion with a number and a falsifiable reason. Proposed criteria at `RA-AC05`–`RA-AC07`.

---

### DRA-5 · Weld genealogy — `FR-160`–`FR-175`, `NFR012`, with `FR-333`, `FR-561`–`FR-568`

**Interpretation.** This is the only **contractual** cluster in the register. A welding-wire customer's
certificate is the deliverable; the chain is `coil alpha → non-overlapping footage ranges → rod alpha →
supplier heat` (`NFR012`, verbatim).

| Aspect | Content |
|---|---|
| **Actors** | FL1/FL3 operator (marks welded, confirms); Supervisor (weld removal, `FR-173`) |
| **Preconditions** | A rod pre-checked-in on the idle bay **and** a rod running on the other (`FR-050`) |
| **Trigger** | *Mark as welded* on the staged bay card (DB2A dialog; DB4 retired 1 Aug 2026) |
| **Inputs** | Outgoing alpha (auto), weld-point footage (**auto from the encoder, never typed** — `FR-162`), incoming alpha (defaults to the staged rod, overridable — `FR-163`), weld type (**Induction only** — `FR-166`), quality Pass/Fail + fail reason (`FR-167`) |
| **Outputs** | `WeldEvent` with both alphas, both payoff positions, footage, type, quality, operator, **server-side timestamp** (`FR-174`) · the run's active-rod pointer advances · weld-pending cleared · a weld marker queued for the gauge trace · `PayoffWeight` re-established |
| **Validations** | Alloy, diameter and temper match the current coil (`FR-164`) · the coil is planned for the current order and compatible with the active schedule (`FR-165`) · joint count within the customer maximum (`FR-171`) |
| **Exception handling** | Quality **Fail** still logs the event and links the rods, flags for supervisor review, may pause or alert — **it does not silently block the run** (`FR-168`). The confirmed event is **immutable**; corrections go through a separate audit flow |

**Issues — five, and the contractual chain does not currently close.**

1. ⛔ **`NFR012`'s chain terminates in a field with no source.** `Rod.SupplierHeat` has **no source
   anywhere** — `proddb..coils` has no heat column and no check-in or staging payload carries one
   (`OI-117`). **The contractual deliverable is specified end-to-end and cannot be produced end-to-end.**
2. ⛔ **`FR-171`'s limit is TBD** (`OI-59`) and `G89` records that a customer weld-count specification
   **has no field anywhere** — raised by the client against his own applications. A `Must` validation
   with no threshold and nowhere to hold one.
3. ⛔ **`FR-563` is blocked on `Q87`** — what a multi-rod coil actually prints was deferred by the client
   on 24 Aug 2026. `G53`: *nothing yet specifies what the label and certificate print.*
4. ⚠ **`OI-127` — the recorded weld footage and the material boundary are captured at different
   moments**, and nothing states whether they coincide. The encoder is read when the operator makes the
   join **at the payoff**; the join passes the counter later. `CoilTraceability` bounds its segments at
   the **material** boundary. Every footage-attributed weight in `FR-170` and `FR-333` inherits this.
5. ⚠ **`OI-25` — weld footage and coil footage are in two different coordinate systems with no stated
   offset**, so *"any run producing more than one coil will build wrong traceability rows."*
6. ⚠ **`FR-173`'s reversal flow is not specified.** The requirement says so itself.
7. ⚠ **`FR-175` has no host** since DB4 was retired (`G27`) — the traceability chain display and the
   re-sequenceable Rods In Queue table moved nowhere.

---

### DRA-6 · SPC checkpoints and SPC-HOLD — `FR-180`–`FR-197`, with `FR-192`, `FR-274`

**Interpretation.** SPC is a **gate**, not a report. It gates check-in (`FR-069`), the stop transaction
(`FR-192`, `FR-274`), resumption after a die change (`FR-185`, `FR-228`) and spool alpha issue
(`FR-157`). Its defining behavioural rule is unusual and deliberate: **out-of-spec suspends the material
and does not stop the machine** (`FR-187`).

| Aspect | Content |
|---|---|
| **Actors** | Any operator (measure, submit); QA (disposition held material, `FR-189`) |
| **Checkpoint types (persisted)** | **Five** — `PreRun`, `PostDieChange`, `ManualSpotCheck`, `PostRun`, `RollAdjustTrigger` (`FR-184`) |
| **Business rules** | Automatic gauge readings are primary; manual entry only at setup and die changes (`FR-182`) · **force-continue is available at all times** (`FR-186`) · out-of-spec → SPC-HOLD, **machine keeps producing** (`FR-187`) · held material cannot advance, ship or release until QA lifts it (`FR-188`) · the operator/footage/timestamp stamp is **immutable**, and footage is captured when the checkpoint **opens** (`FR-191`) |
| **Outputs** | `SpcCheckpoint` + `SpcMeasurement` rows; CPK per run excluding unstable start and end regions (`FR-190`) |

**Issues.**

1. ⛔ **SPC-HOLD has no column** — `OI-23`. The single most behaviourally distinctive state in the
   quality model has no persistence. `FR-187`, `FR-188` and `FR-189` all operate on it.
2. ⛔ **Published tolerance bands per alloy and temper are undefined** — `OI-57`. *"Without them SPC
   control limits cannot be configured."* `FR-193`'s tolerance-band visualisation, `FR-194`'s danger
   elevation and every in/out-of-spec badge depend on a number nobody has supplied.
3. ⛔ **An SPC checkpoint cannot join to its trigger** — `OI-18`: no `DieChangeId` / `OverrideId` foreign
   key. `FR-196` requires the checkpoint to display a trigger banner naming the die block and the size
   change; `FR-210` requires the DB11 measurements to land as a `RollAdjustTrigger` checkpoint. Neither
   can be reconstructed from the data.
4. ⛔ **`G51` — `SpcMeasurement.InSpec` stores a wrong answer for an asymmetric tolerance, and stores it
   on disk.** `FR-065` explicitly permits asymmetric bands. The computed column uses a symmetric
   `ABS(actual − target)` test.
5. ⚠ **`FR-184`'s enum and the UI disagree** — the UI additionally offers **Post DB1** (`OI-10`).
6. ⚠ **`FR-190`'s "defined stable process window" is not defined.** No requirement, register entry or
   schema object states the exclusion boundaries. Raised as `RA-AMB07`.

---

### DRA-7 · The three checkout modes — `FR-300`–`FR-327`, `FR-052`–`FR-053a`, `[EX §4.6]`

**Interpretation.** Four modes exist, not three: **Mode P** (pre-check-out, never checked in), **Mode A**
(pre-run, footage 0), **Mode B** (mid-run, footage > 0), and the **WIP-rejection release** of a `BLOCKED`
bay (`FR-053a`), which is *"the only thing that clears a `BLOCKED` bay"*.

| | **Mode P** | **Mode A** | **Mode B** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Checked in? | No | Yes | Yes |
| `RunId` | NULL | NULL | populated |
| Footage | 0 | 0 | > 0 |
| PLC tags | **none pushed** | cleared | cleared **after confirmed stop** |
| Line-state gate | **not needed** | yes | yes |
| Approval | Operator; **welded → Supervisor + PIN + reason, rod → `HOLD`** (`FR-052a`) | Operator | **Supervisor** (`FR-323`) |
| Screen | DB2A | DB12 | DB12, **only** via the Pause dialog (`FR-320`) |
| Resulting rod status | `RECEIVED` or `STAGED` | `STAGED` or `RECEIVED` | `HOLD`, `SCRAP` or `STAGED` |

**The PLC gatekeeper rule (all modes with tags).** Read `FL{n}.LineState` **before the dialog opens and
before a confirm is accepted**; block while Running; **never send a stop command**; read and **lock the
footage counter at the moment the dialog opens** (`FR-301`–`FR-303`).

**Issues.**

1. ⛔ **`G7` — Mode B's supervisor approval relies on a transient SignalR notification.** If no
   supervisor is connected, the approval is lost and **the material stays locked with no alpha**
   (`FR-324`, `FR-326`). A **durable pending-approval queue** is required, with SignalR as a live nudge
   only. The register states the need; nothing implements it.
2. ⛔ **`OI-32` — there is no endpoint for the supervisor disposition command.** `FR-325`'s
   Accept/Hold/Reject has no API surface.
3. ⛔ **`FR-301`'s gate reads a vocabulary nobody has documented** — `OI-35`. Two-state run/stop bit, or
   `RUNNING / STOPPED / PAUSED / FAULT / THREADING / JOG`? Two features depend on it: this gatekeeper
   and the spool stop-confirmation (`FR-141`).
4. ⚠ **`FR-323` requires supervisor approval; `D-52` says MVP-1 does not authorise.** The approval is
   collected and displayed but **not enforced by any policy** — any authenticated caller can act as the
   supervisor. See `RA-CON05`.
5. ⚠ **Carry-forward is specified in `[EX §4.7]` and is thinly represented in the register.** `FR-043`
   carries the DOM rule; the rest — *a new independent run record with footage at zero, each segment
   producing its own spool alpha, material left in the mill scrapped and not carried forward* — is in
   `[EX]` only. Raised as `RA-G05`.

### DRA-8 · Output coil completion and the skid rule — `FR-330`–`FR-340`, `FR-509`–`FR-518`, `FR-561`–`FR-570`

**Interpretation.** DB7's *Confirm & Move to Packing* is the transaction that produces the
customer-facing deliverable **and** the shared-schema record set. It is the most heavily amended cluster
in the register: §5.30 (26 Aug 2026) re-specifies seven of §5.25's ten requirements and deletes one.

| Aspect | Content |
|---|---|
| **Actors** | FL2 / FL3 operator; downstream: packing, shipping, certification, cost and yield |
| **Trigger** | Coil completion on DB7 |
| **Key business rules** | Alpha `FW-#####-C##` (`FR-330`) · **target dimensions displayed when SPC confirms in-tolerance**, measured only when out (`FR-331`) · net weight **derived, never scaled during rolling** (`FR-332`) · **exactly two coreless coils per skid**, counted in **physical** coils (`FR-335` + `FR-570`) · package OD, width and weight validated against order constraints (`FR-337`) · the **schedule snapshot** written to the coil record and **not printed on the label** (`FR-338`) |
| **Shared-schema effects** | One coil identity **per source rod** (`FR-561`) · one coil row, order link, cost record, cut record and WIP transaction **per part** (`FR-510`–`FR-516` as amended) · skid opened on the first coil and closed on the second (`FR-515`) · **all or nothing** (`FR-518`), with the retry contract as the **set** of identities (`FR-569`) |

**Issues — six.**

1. ⛔ **`G54` (Critical) — the 26 Aug alpha design has an unbuilt precondition.** *Nothing registers an
   FL1 segment alpha in `proddb..coils`*, so every mint passes a blank. `FR-561` cannot execute.
2. ⛔ **`FR-570` amends a `[CONFIRMED]` requirement with `[PROPOSED]` text and needs client
   re-sign-off** — together with `FR-335`, `FR-339`, `FR-515`. **The skid rule is currently in two
   states at once.**
3. ⛔ **`FR-336` / `FR-563` blocked on `Q87`** — see `DRA-5`.
4. ⛔ **`lotNumber` is returned by the label endpoint and printed, and has no column and no generator**
   — `OI-24`. `FR-330` and `FR-336` both require it.
5. ⚠ **`OI-25` — two footage coordinate systems**, so any run producing more than one coil builds wrong
   traceability rows (`FR-333`).
6. ⚠ **Coreless coil OD/ID limits are pending** — `OI-65` — which `FR-337`'s validation needs.

### DRA-9 · Rod ↔ order allocation and the mounted handoff — `FR-541`–`FR-560`

**Interpretation.** This is the newest and most structurally consequential cluster: it changes what a
*run* means. Because a rod stays mounted across an order boundary and is checked in once, **one run spans
two orders** — and the schema forces it, since a check-in points at exactly one run.

| Aspect | Content |
|---|---|
| **Cardinality** | Rod 1—many Order · Spool 1—many Rod · Spool 1—many Order · FL2 output — **exactly one order at a time** |
| **Sequencing** | Four tiers: pinned-first · free full · free partial · pinned-last. Legal sequence count `\|free full\|! × \|free partial\|!`. **A rod may be pinned at both ends** |
| **Split point** | Held in **pounds, not footage** — weight is conserved through drawing and rolling and footage is not (900 lb ≈ 11,100 ft at FL1 gauge, ≈ 76,300 ft at FL2) |
| **Handoff** | Notify on reaching the allocated weight (`FR-551`) → operator marks the order complete (`FR-552`) → next order begins **on the same mount**. The interval between crossing and acknowledgement is a **recorded state** and the **overrun is persisted, not discarded** (`FR-553`) |

**Issues.**

1. ⛔ **`FR-546` and `FR-045` give opposite answers to the same question.** `FR-045`: an out-of-sequence
   rod is *"notify and require supervisor authorisation — **never refuse**"*. `FR-546`: a rod presented
   out of tier order is *"**refused** — not offered as an authorised override"*. Both are `Must`, both
   apply at pre-check-in and check-in. **See `RA-CON06` — this is the sharpest direct contradiction in
   the register.**
2. ⛔ **`FR-044` is knowingly wrong** and the register says so: the different-order refusal breaks a
   same-rod successor order (`G22`, `OQ-73`).
3. ⛔ **`G47` / `OI-123` — `FlatWireRun.OrderId` is read as "the order this run produced" and stops
   being that at a boundary.** Anything reading it that way is **silently wrong**.
4. ⛔ **`G48` / `OI-124` — the order boundary is lost at the spool hop.** A spool wound across a
   boundary records *that* it carries two orders and **not where the boundary is**; FL2 must cut at that
   point and cannot compute it.
5. ⚠ **`FR-543` requires enforcement "as a database constraint rather than an application check
   alone"** — an implementation directive inside a requirement. Correct in intent; it belongs in the
   design, and stating it here makes the requirement untestable at the behavioural level.
6. ⚠ **`FR-561d` and `FR-561e` both state, in the requirement text, that they cannot be enforced** —
   *"Not expressible as a database constraint"*, *"No foreign key can enforce this"*. They are
   requirements on the **test suite**, and should be labelled as such.

---

### DRA-10 · Line status alerts — `FR-420`–`FR-428`

**Interpretation.** DB1 is the floor master board and the first live end-to-end slice (Phase 3:
OPC → hub → dashboard). The five alert rules in `FR-423` are stated exactly and are the only
enumerated rules engine in the register.

**Issues.**

1. ⛔ **`OI-28` — the alert lifecycle is unbacked, and it blocks Phase 3.** `AlertRaised` /
   `AlertCleared`, the `activeAlerts` payload and the five rules all exist; **no table stores an alert**
   and no story implements raise, clear or acknowledgement persistence. Consequence, stated in source:
   *"Alerts cannot survive a restart and acknowledgements cannot be audited."* `FR-428` requires
   per-alert acknowledgement with an acknowledged count — **unbuildable**.
2. ⚠ **`FR-421` requires "live gauge and width for FL1 and FL3, blank for FL2 when idle."** Two
   readings are possible — *blank because FL2 is idle* or *blank because FL2 never broadcasts* — and
   `Q19`/`G120` now makes the difference material. Raised as `RA-AMB09`.
3. ⚠ **`FR-427` requires die life percentages and the active pass schedule ID** on an MVP-1 board;
   die life comes from **MVP-2** Die Management (`FR-254`) and the schedule from **MVP-2** DB9.
   See `RA-CON01`.
4. ✅ **`FR-424` is a model requirement and should be cited as the pattern.** It names the data source,
   states why the obvious alternative is wrong (*"`PayoffWeight` alone cannot distinguish an empty bay
   from a sensor reading zero"*), and names the event that keeps the evaluation live. Every ambiguity in
   this report would be smaller if more requirements were written this way.

an `OI-##` register. Where a gap is already registered, its id is used and **no `RA-G##` is minted**.
Only findings this analysis raises that have no existing id get an `RA-G##`.

## 7. Missing Scenarios

Scenarios the register does not cover. Each is stated as the condition, not as a proposed requirement.

### 7.1 Happy-path gaps

| ID | Missing scenario | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| `RA-MS01` | **The FL1 → furnace → FL2 hop.** `FR-276` routes the spool to a furnace for annealing; no requirement covers dispatch, the furnace queue, return, or the status the spool carries while it is there | The transition between the two in-scope lines. `[BR §3.5]` says an intermediate anneal **modifies the existing alpha** — a rule with no requirement (`RA-G06`) |
| `RA-MS02` | **First-ever run on a cold system.** `FR-038` covers a cold *line*; nothing covers a cold *database* — no pass schedules, no dies, no scrap boxes, no spools | Every check-in precondition is an existence assumption. `OI-110`: the pass schedule tables are *"populated by nobody"* |
| `RA-MS03` | **A run that produces exactly one coil, and one that produces three.** `FR-335`'s skid rule is written for pairs; `FR-515` refuses a third coil on a skid. What closes a skid holding one coil at end of shift or end of order is unstated | Skids will strand. `FR-351` closes on the second coil only |
| `RA-MS04` | **Order completion when the last rod is exhausted exactly at the allocation.** `FR-551`–`FR-553` describe the overrun case; the zero-overrun case is not described | The boundary condition of a new `Must` cluster |

### 7.2 Alternative-flow gaps

| ID | Missing scenario | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| `RA-MS05` | **Shift change mid-run.** No requirement states whether a run, an open pause, an open SPC checkpoint or an unacknowledged milestone survives a shift boundary — while *shift changeover* is an enumerated pause reason | `RA-G13`. Certain to occur daily |
| `RA-MS06` | **Two operators on one line.** `FR-005` associates operators to runs; nothing arbitrates two operators answering one stop prompt, acknowledging one milestone or applying two roll adjusts | `RA-G08`. `OI-75` covers the stop popup only |
| `RA-MS07` | **An open MMS ID on an aborted run or a Mode B checkout.** `FR-013` closes strictly on consumption, which never fires | `RA-G04`. Feeds `FR-009`'s ITInhibit condition |
| `RA-MS08` | **A rod that fails inspection *after* being checked in.** `FR-041`/`FR-068` block at staging and at check-in; `FR-292` disposes in-process material. Nothing covers the rod itself being found bad post-acknowledgement with footage 0 | Mode A exists for this but its reason list (`FR-311`) has no *failed inspection* entry; `FR-052`'s does |
| `RA-MS09` | **A pass schedule deactivated while a run is using it.** `FR-375` offers **Deactivate**; `FR-338` snapshots the configuration at coil creation, not at check-in | A run could be executing a schedule no longer `Active` |
| `RA-MS10` | **Partial re-check-in of a rod onto a *different* line.** `FR-052`'s reasons include *"Relocated to different line"*; `[EX §4.7]` says re-check-in retrieves the existing record by alpha and opens a new run. Whether the carry-forward crosses lines is unstated | FL1 and FL3 share rod payoffs; the footage basis differs |

### 7.3 Exception, failure and recovery gaps

| ID | Missing scenario | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| `RA-MS11` | **PLC unreachable at check-in** (as distinct from a tag write failing) | `RA-G09`. The most likely production failure |
| `RA-MS12` | **Compensating writes themselves fail.** `FR-074` re-clears already-written tags on failure; nothing covers the re-clear failing | The recovery path has no recovery path. Feeds `OI-39` |
| `RA-MS13` | **Database available, hub down.** `NFR006`/`FR-119` cover the *client* losing transport. Nothing covers the *server* being unable to broadcast while transactions still commit | Operators act on stale state that the system believes was delivered |
| `RA-MS14` | **One of the two FL3 data-collection instances fails** (`FR-016`) | `RA-G14` |
| `RA-MS15` | **A duplicate submit of any transaction** — double-tap on a touch panel with gloves. Only `FR-549` (duplicate rod scan) addresses duplication, and only for check-in | Gloved operation on a touch panel is an explicit operating condition (`[REQ §2.4]`) |
| `RA-MS16` | **A supervisor rejects a Mode B disposition and the operator disputes it.** `FR-325`'s Accept/Hold/Reject is terminal; no appeal, correction or reversal path exists, and `FR-326` routes Reject to scrap | Material is scrapped on a single unappealable decision |
| `RA-MS17` | **QA lifts an SPC-HOLD after the coil has been packed.** `FR-188` blocks advancement, shipping and release; `FR-351` closes the skid and moves it to staging | The two lifecycles are not sequenced against each other |
| `RA-MS18` | **A weld is recorded and the incoming rod then fails to feed.** `FR-168` keeps a failed *weld quality* non-blocking; nothing covers a *physically failed* weld discovered downstream | `FR-173`'s reversal flow *"is not yet specified"* |
| `RA-MS19` | **Clock skew or timezone at a shift boundary.** `FR-174` mandates server-side timestamps; no requirement states the timezone, and `FR-486` computes utilisation against shift windows | Shift reports at DST boundaries |
| `RA-MS20` | **Label printer offline at commit.** `FR-146` prints labels *after* the transaction commits, so the transaction is already durable when printing fails | No reprint requirement exists anywhere in the register |

### 7.4 Boundary and data gaps

| ID | Missing scenario | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| `RA-MS21` | **Rod with `footageRunToDate` equal to its full length** — a fully consumed rod re-presented at staging. `FR-043` handles > 0; the exhausted case is not distinguished | `[BR]`'s `INFLAT → COMPLETE` transition is *"rod exhausted naturally"*, with no staging guard |
| `RA-MS22` | **Zero-length or negative-delta values** — `FR-204`'s delta on every keystroke, `FR-271`'s Rod Buildup range, `FR-151`'s gross scale weight below tare | Touch-panel numeric entry with no stated lower bounds |
| `RA-MS23` | **Spool with `OrderNo` null at completion** rather than at queue time. `FR-099` explicitly permits an unallocated spool in the queue; `FR-098` resolves an order server-side | An unallocated spool reaching completion has no order to link |
| `RA-MS24` | **More than two source rods on one coil.** `FR-561`–`FR-568` are written for *N* but every worked example is two, and `FR-563`'s label render (`Q87`) is framed as *"one alpha or two"* | The label has no stated width limit |

## 8. Dependencies

### 8.1 Internal (within this module)

| Dependency | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Pass Schedule → everything** | Phase 2 is *"the highest dependency in the project"*; it blocks all check-in and PLC work. ⚠ Its authoring screens are **MVP-2** (`RA-CON01`) |
| **Real-time backbone → 5 phases** | Phase 3 (DB1 + hub + OPC poller) is consumed by Phases 4, 5, 6, 8, 9 |
| **Check-in → active run → in-run events → exceptions** | 4 → 5 → 6 → 7, strictly sequential |
| **FL1 output → FL2 input** | Phase 8 needs an FL1-produced spool. ⚠ `G37`: *nothing creates the `SpoolProcessing` row* |
| **Coil completion → FL3 hybrid** | Phase 10 depends on 4, 5, 6 and 9 — **not on Phase 8**; FL3 has no intermediate spool |
| **Die inventory → Die Change** | `Q91` moved `ToolingInventoryDie` into Phase 1, so **Phase 6 depends on Phase 1**, not Phase 13 |
| **Staging → line status** | `FR-424`: the *"Payoff 2 not loaded"* alert has **no other data source** than `RodStaging` |

|---|---|---|---|
| **CoilReceiving** | In | `R#####` rod rows in `coils` with valid chemistry and weight | Out of test scope, fixture-supplied. `OI-49`: inventory type for rod entries is TBD |
| **Planning** | In | `planning_routings` allocation; **the rod ↔ order pairing, per-pairing weight and planned sequence** (`FR-542`) | `FR-098` cannot resolve an order unless `SpoolProcessing.OrderNo` is populated from planning |
| **Scheduling** | In | Order → line booking, operation letter `F` | `OI-27`: no `F` case in the op-letter map. `G86`: the committed analysis assigns **two operation letters already in use** |
| **`Login`** | In | JWT with six roles on `ClaimTypes.Role` | ✅ Confirmed 15 Aug 2026. ⚠ Residual: the claim **values** are coded and unmapped (`G6`); `FW-177` targets SignalR groups by role name and **fails silent** |
| **`OPCConnection`** | Both | Tag read (speed, feet, line state, weights) and tag write (the push) | ⛔ `G58`: reports no write failure. `G95`: returns an empty list for a line with no system-error tag row. `G96`: the module-id constant is stale |
| **Shared `coils` / `wip_stations` / `planning_routings` / `routings`** | Both | Read as they stand; **written, never altered** (`D-32`) | `OI-39`: no recovery path. `Q37`–`Q40` need IT sign-off on tokens and status values |

## 9. Assumptions

### 9.1 Stated assumptions (from `[REQ §2.6]`)

| Assumption | Consequence if false | Current standing |
|---|---|---|
| A rod exists in `coils` with a `planning_routings` allocation before it reaches the line | Staging and check-in refuse it; the line has no material | Holds. `FR-529`–`FR-532` now project the local record from it |
| An `Active` pass schedule exists for the alloy + line + target combination | Check-in has no schedule to acknowledge; **the no-match path is undefined** | ⛔ `OI-46` open, and `RA-CON01` makes the authoring screens MVP-2 |
| ~~The six roles exist as JWT claims in `Login`~~ | ~~Authorisation blocks the build~~ | ✅ Confirmed 15 Aug 2026. ⚠ Residual: claim **values** coded and unmapped |
| PLC tag paths are confirmed at commissioning | Simulated push covers development; go-live is gated | Holds; `[PLC]` is v1.0 with no `[CONFIRMED]` tag **by design** |

### 9.2 Assumptions this analysis infers — each needs confirmation

| ID | Inferred assumption | Basis | If wrong |
|---|---|---|---|
| `RA-ASM01` | **A pass schedule is authored outside MVP-1's delivered UI** — seeded, or created in the web application | `RA-CON01`; `FR-360` says the table is *"accessible from both the shopfloor and the web applications"* | MVP-1 cannot check a rod in at all |
| `RA-ASM02` | **The `Q10` nominal basis applies retroactively to nothing** — no historical weight is recomputed | `FR-556`'s additive re-planning and *"a later answer to `Q10` cannot retro-change a historical record"* | Existing seeded weights are inconsistent with new ones |
| `RA-ASM03` | **"Two coils per skid" means two *finished FL2* coils**, never an FL1 spool | `FR-277`, `FR-335`; never stated as an exclusion | FL1 output could be skidded by the same rule |
| `RA-ASM04` | **An operator is physically present at every transaction** | Every dialog requires a confirm; no unattended path exists | An unattended overnight run has no defined behaviour |
| `RA-ASM05` | **The touch panel is the only client for operator transactions**; supervisor and maintenance surfaces are desktop | `[REQ §2.4]` lists them separately | A supervisor approving from a phone (`FR-046`'s remote fallback) has no specified client |
| `RA-ASM06` | **`FL{n}.LineState` is readable at all times, including while the line is faulted** | `FR-301` blocks a checkout on *"Running"*, implying every other value permits it | A `FAULT` value would silently permit a checkout on a faulted line |
| `RA-ASM07` | **One skid is open per line at a time** | `FR-515` opens on the first coil and closes on the second, with no skid selector | Two lines completing coils concurrently could contend for one skid |
| `RA-ASM08` | **The register's `Must` on a `[PROPOSED]` requirement means "must, if the proposal is accepted"** | 69 requirements are `[PROPOSED]` **and** `Must` | 69 `Must` requirements are being planned as commitments on unreviewed text |
| `RA-ASM09` | **`FR-018`'s cadence configuration is per line, not global** | *"FL2 always 4 ft; FL3 hybrid — both instances 4 ft"* implies per-instance | A global setting cannot express the stated rule |
| `RA-ASM10` | **Withdrawn requirement numbers are never reused, including by the MVP-2 document** | `[REQ]`'s *"numbers retained, never reused"* | A collision would silently corrupt traceability |

## 10. Acceptance Criteria

### 10.1 Extracted — criteria the sources already state testably

The register states acceptance-grade criteria inline more often than most. The strongest, quoted or
closely paraphrased, are:

| Ref | Extracted criterion |
|---|---|
| `FR-072` | **Given** a check-in acknowledgement, **when** the PLC push is attempted, **then** the visual-inspection result, Pre-Run SPC checkpoint, schedule ID + version + effective date, and the acknowledgement event are **already persisted**; **and** if that write fails, an incomplete-push recovery marker is retained |
| `FR-074` | **Given** a batch push in which any individual tag write fails, **then** tags already written are re-cleared by compensating write, shared-schema changes are reverted, and the check-in is aborted |
| `FR-041` | **Given** any inspection item marked Fail, **then** there is **no** control that proceeds to check-in; the only forward action is WIP Rejection |
| `FR-043` | **Given** `footageRunToDate > 0`, **then** the fresh-start control **does not exist in the DOM** (not merely disabled) |
| `FR-013` | **Given** an MMS ID, **when** remaining ft reaches 0, **then** it closes; **and** no operator action closes it under any circumstance |
| `FR-051` | **Given** a rod marked welded, **then** no bay switch occurs; **when** consumption reaches 0 ft, **then** the payoff transition occurs |
| `FR-149` | **Given** the stop-confirmation question step, **when** Escape or click-outside occurs, **then** the dialog does not dismiss; **and** `Y` and `N` are accepted and advertised |
| `FR-153` | **Given** a variance beyond tolerance, **then** the commit control is **never disabled**; an override panel appears and the button relabels |
| `FR-155` | **Given** any completion, **then** both weights and the variance are persisted **regardless of which basis is chosen**; **and** the PIN is not in the payload |
| `FR-174` | **Given** any event, **then** the persisted timestamp is the server-side timestamp at API receipt, not the client clock |
| `FR-191` | **Given** an SPC checkpoint, **then** footage is captured at **open**, not at submit; **and** the operator/footage/timestamp stamp cannot be modified |
| `FR-211` | **Given** all roll-gap deltas are zero, **then** Apply reads *"No changes — return to run"* and **no record is written** |
| `FR-231` | **Given** Cancel on the die-change dialog, **then** no record is written and the run is unpaused |
| `FR-332a` | **Given** 1100 at 0.110″ × 0.625″, **then** lb/ft is **0.0809** (square) or **0.0778** (round); **and** `0.069` is never produced |
| `FR-424` | **Given** an empty payoff bay and a sensor reading of zero, **then** the *"Payoff 2 not loaded"* evaluation distinguishes them, because it reads `RodStaging`, not `PayoffWeight` |
| `FR-530` | **Given** a rod retrieval for display, **then** no record is created or modified |
| `NFR005` | **Given** a 5-minute run, **when** the network trace is examined, **then** it shows **zero** polling requests |
| `NFR006` | **Given** transport loss mid-run, **then** cached state renders within one frame with a "Reconnecting…" banner, backoff reconnect occurs, and the line group is re-joined automatically |

### 10.2 Proposed — supported by the sources, **not** in them

⚠ **These are proposals. No business rule has been added to make a criterion complete.** Each cites the
requirement it is derived from; none introduces a threshold, role or behaviour the sources do not state.

| ID | For | Proposed criterion |
|---|---|---|
| `RA-AC01` | `FR-070` | **Given** a rod whose attribute combination matches **no** `Active` schedule, **when** check-in is attempted, **then** the system does **X** — ⛔ **X cannot be proposed.** `OI-46` is a business decision, not a derivation. Recorded here so the untestable path is visible |
| `RA-AC02` | `FR-073` | **Given** an acknowledgement, **then** exactly one tag batch is issued per acknowledgement, and the audit log holds one entry per tag with path, value, operator, timestamp and result |
| `RA-AC03` | `FR-074` | **Given** the compensating re-clear itself fails, **then** the failure is surfaced and the run is not left `Running` — ⚠ **derived, and `RA-MS12` shows the source is silent** |
| `RA-AC04` | `FR-083` | **Given** an FL3 acknowledgement, **then** FM1 and FM2 tags are pushed within one operator action, and **no** `SpoolProcessing` row exists for that run |
| `RA-AC05` | `FR-137` | **Given** 1100 at nominal 0.110″ × 0.625″ over 24,900 ft, **then** the derived spool weight is 2,014 lb ± 1 lb, using ρ from `united_db..alloys.alloy_density` |
| `RA-AC06` | `FR-137` | **Given** the same run, **when** the dimensional basis is the `Q10` answer (**nominal**), **then** the recorded basis and factor are persisted on the consumption record (`FR-556`) |
| `RA-AC07` | `FR-153` | **Given** a coil fully in spec at the tolerance extremes (gauge +0.002, width −0.005), **then** the computed variance is reported and — ⚠ **on the current ±2 % threshold it exceeds tolerance.** This criterion is written to **fail** deliberately, as the evidence for `CF-2` |
| `RA-AC08` | `FR-009` | **Given** a normal weld transition on a healthy line, **then** ITInhibit does **not** set — ⚠ depends on `RA-AMB03` |
| `RA-AC09` | `FR-008` | **Given** ITInhibit set on FL1, **then** FL2 and FL3 continue to run — ⚠ derived from `[TS §2.3]`, **not** from `[REQ]` (`RA-G03`) |
| `RA-AC10` | `FR-187` | **Given** an out-of-spec SPC submission, **then** the machine continues producing **and** the affected output is on SPC-HOLD — ⛔ **untestable until `OI-23` gives SPC-HOLD a column** |
| `RA-AC11` | `FR-292` | **Given** a `Rework` disposition, **then** the material status and the return stage are both persisted — ⛔ **untestable until `OI-22` is resolved** |
| `RA-AC12` | `FR-324` | **Given** a Mode B submission with **no supervisor connected**, **then** the pending approval survives and is delivered when one connects — ⚠ derived from `G7`; the source specifies only a transient notification |
| `RA-AC13` | `FR-335` | **Given** a coil produced from two source rods, **then** it occupies **one** of the skid's two slots — the `FR-570` physical-coil basis. ⚠ **`[PROPOSED]`, pending client re-sign-off** |
| `RA-AC14` | `NFR012` | **Given** a completed multi-rod coil, **then** the traceability chain resolves coil alpha → footage ranges (covering the full length, non-overlapping) → rod alphas → supplier heat — ⛔ **the last hop is untestable; `OI-117`, supplier heat has no source** |
| `RA-AC15` | `FR-546` / `FR-045` | **Given** an out-of-sequence rod at staging, **then** — ⛔ **no criterion can be written.** The two requirements demand opposite outcomes (`RA-CON06`) |
| `RA-AC16` | `FR-120` / `FR-421` | **Given** FL2 running standalone, **then** the dashboard shows — ⛔ **no criterion can be written** until `G120` is resolved |

> **Six of the sixteen proposed criteria are deliberately unwritable**, and that is the finding: they
> mark exactly where the register cannot be tested, not where the analysis ran out of effort.

## 12. Risks

| ID | Risk | Cause | Impact | Severity | Affected requirements | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `RA-R01` | **A wrong pass-schedule push configures the machine wrongly and produces wrong product at line speed** | `FR-074` cannot detect a failed write (`G58`); no recovery path (`OI-39`); FL3 writes two controllers with nothing specified (`G99`) | Scrap at production volume; a wrong product shipped under a correct certificate | **Critical** | `FR-070`–`FR-075`, `FR-083` | Fix the `OPCConnection` interface **or** re-specify `FR-074` against observable state. Decide the recovery model before Phase 4 |
| `RA-R02` | **The welding-wire certificate cannot be produced, or is produced wrong** | Supplier heat has no source (`OI-117`); two footage coordinate systems (`OI-25`); the encoder read and the material boundary are different moments (`OI-127`); `Q87` blocks the render | **Contractual failure.** `NFR012` is a customer obligation, not an internal goal | **Critical** | `FR-172`, `FR-333`, `FR-563`, `NFR012` | Close `OI-117`, `OI-25` and `Q87` before the first certificate is owed. Test the chain with a **multi-rod, multi-coil** run, not a single-rod one |
| `RA-R03` | **Every weight in the system is wrong by a consistent factor** | The `Q10` basis has just changed and the requirements still say "open"; `FR-153`'s threshold is arithmetically unreachable; `Q93` finds the client's own formulas split between square- and round-edge area | Yield, cost, order consumption, spool milestones and customer weights all move together, so the error is **self-consistent and hard to spot** | **Critical** | `FR-015`, `FR-137`, `FR-332`, `FR-153`, `FR-559` | Propagate the `Q10` answer into the requirement text and close `OI-45`. Add `RA-AC05`'s worked figure as a regression assertion |
| `RA-R04` | **MVP-1 ships unable to check a rod in** | The pass-schedule authoring screens are MVP-2 and nothing populates the tables (`RA-CON01`, `OI-110`) | The core operator journey is undeliverable | **Critical** | `FR-070`, `FR-360`–`FR-410` | Answer `RA-Q01` now. Either pull a minimal authoring path into MVP-1 or commit to a seeded schedule set |
| `RA-R05` | **69 `Must` requirements are built from unreviewed text and are rejected at UAT** | §5.25–§5.30 are `[PROPOSED]`; `Q41` (`Critical`) is open under all of §5.29 | Late rework on the shared-schema write-back, the allocation model and the coil identity design — the three most structurally coupled areas | **Critical** | `FR-509`–`FR-570` | Get §5.25–§5.30 client-reviewed as a block, before Phase 9 |
| `RA-R06` | **The client believes authorisation is delivered when it is not** | Six columns of ticks in `[SEC §8]`; `D-52` defers all of it | A supervisor-approval control that anyone can operate, presented as a control | **High** | `FR-212`, `FR-323`, `FR-361`, `FR-367`, `FR-410`, `FR-490` | Raise `RA-Q09` explicitly at the next client review, as `[SEC]` itself asks |
| `RA-R07` | **Alerts and approvals are lost on restart or when nobody is connected** | No alert store (`OI-28`); Mode B approval is transient SignalR only (`G7`) | Material locked with no alpha and no one notified; unauditable acknowledgements | **High** | `FR-324`, `FR-325`, `FR-422`, `FR-428` | Durable queue + alert table. Both are schema additions, cheapest now |
| `RA-R08` | **The 30 September date is met by descoping on derived priorities** | Only two groups carry a stated business priority (`RA-AMB01`); `G1` is the capacity escalation; `OI-51` requires *"an explicit programme decision"* | The wrong things are cut, and nobody notices until UAT | **High** | All `Should`/`Could` | Answer `RA-Q07`. Have the client rank the descope-ladder candidates |
| `RA-R09` | **Rod tolerance is seeded with wrong data** | `Q22`'s values arrived at a grain the table cannot hold (`G121`) | A validation that silently passes or fails the wrong rods, at the first gate in the process | **High** | `FR-042`, `FR-065` | Do **not** seed per-alloy. Re-grain first |
| `RA-R10` | **FL2 is built to the wrong data model** | `G120` — six documents say `null`, the client says live | The FL2 route's dashboard, weight derivation and trace all branch on it | **High** | `FR-120`, `FR-137`, `FR-421`, `FR-093` | Ask `RA-Q04` directly. **Change nothing until answered** — the current text is at least self-consistent |
| `RA-R11` | **Requirement coverage cannot be proven at UAT** | Three requirement totals (`RA-CON02`); `G25` already found 41 requirements with no test case | The release gate asserts coverage that cannot be demonstrated | **High** | All | Re-run the generator (`RA-Q47`) and rebuild the coverage matrix from the document, not from a range table |

## 14. Final Assessment

### 14.1 Overall quality

**Above the norm for a specification of this size, and below the bar for one of this consequence.**

What is genuinely good, and should not be lost in a rewrite: requirements are grouped by operator
workflow with actors, preconditions, validations, state changes, error paths and real-time events stated
per group; non-functional constraints are folded **inline** into the group they constrain, so a developer
reading check-in sees the audit obligation that applies to check-in; superseded text is retained in place
with the date and the reason, so a reader can reconstruct any decision; and the register is unusually
willing to record its own defects — `FR-044` is marked *"knowingly wrong"*, `FR-153`'s arithmetic is
disproved in a callout beneath it, and `FR-280`–`FR-282` are labelled *"not implementable as written"*.
**That candour is the reason this analysis could be as specific as it is.**

What is not good enough: the register **cannot state its own size** (three totals), **carries 69 `Must`
requirements nobody outside the delivery team has read**, **specifies authorisation it will not enforce**,
and **has not absorbed client answers that arrived on the day of this analysis and contradict standing
text**.

### 14.2 Completeness

| Dimension | Assessment |
|---|---|
| **Functional coverage** | **Strong.** 424 defined requirements across 24 screens/dashboards, every operator transaction, and the server-side write-backs |
| **Error paths** | **Strong by convention** — every group has an *Error paths* line — **weak on second-order failure**: `RA-MS11`–`RA-MS14` |
| **Data model** | **Strong**, but **nine decided requirements have no column to land in** (`G49`) and four specific ones are named in this report (`OI-22`, `OI-23`, `OI-24`, `G38`) |
| **Non-functional** | **Registered but incomplete.** Ten NFRs with measurable targets and named test cases; **four targets undefined**, and the hub load test *"cannot fail"* |
| **Security** | **Specified, not delivered.** `RA-CON05` |
| **Compliance / retention** | **Weak.** Only `NFR013` states retention. No archival, deletion or operator-identity policy (`RA-G07`) |
| **Concurrency** | **Weak.** `NFR007` covers two dashboards on two lines; nothing covers two operators on one line (`RA-G08`) |
| **Volume / scale** | **Absent.** No screen states an expected row count (`RA-G10`) |

### 14.3 Major blockers

1. **`RA-Q01`** — how an `Active` pass schedule exists in MVP-1, when its authoring screens are MVP-2.
   **This is the one that stops a demonstration, not just a build.**
2. **`OI-46` / `RA-Q02`** — the no-match path at check-in.
3. **`G58`** — `FR-074` cannot observe the condition it is specified against.
4. **`OI-28` / `RA-Q12`** — the alert lifecycle, blocking Phase 3.
5. **`G121` / `RA-Q05`** — rod tolerance grain, blocking Phase 4 seeding.
6. **`Q41`** — open and `Critical`, under all eight of §5.29.
7. **`G54`** — nothing registers an FL1 segment alpha, so `FR-561` cannot execute.
8. **`Q87` / `RA-Q06`** — blocking `FR-563` on the contractual deliverable.
9. **`OI-117` / `RA-Q14`** — supplier heat has no source; `NFR012`'s chain does not close.
10. **`OI-22` / `RA-Q13`** — `Rework` is unpersistable, blocking Phase 7.

### 14.4 Critical risks

`RA-R01` (wrong PLC push), `RA-R02` (certificate failure — **contractual**), `RA-R03` (every weight wrong
by a consistent factor), `RA-R04` (MVP-1 cannot check a rod in), `RA-R05` (69 unreviewed `Must`
requirements).

### 14.6 Recommended next action

**In this order. The first three are the ones that unblock the most.**

1. **Take `RA-Q01`–`RA-Q14` (Critical) to the client as one list.** Nine of the fourteen are already
   registered — this is a chase, not a new discovery exercise.
2. **Propagate the 9 September workbook answers into the requirement text.** `Q10` closes `OI-45`;
   `Q19` and `Q22` open `G120` and `G121` and **must not be silently absorbed**. ⛔ **Edit nothing on
   `Q19`'s strength until `RA-Q04` is answered** — the current text is at least self-consistent.
3. **Get §5.25–§5.30 client-reviewed as a block** — 69 `Must` requirements, the shared-schema
   write-back, the allocation model and the coil identity design.
4. **Re-run `build_coverage_matrix.py` and reconcile the three requirement totals** before any coverage
   claim is made at UAT.
5. **Resolve the four schema holes that block phases** — `OI-22` (Rework), `OI-23` (SPC-HOLD),
   `OI-24` (lot number), `G38` (durable prompt). All four are additive and cheapest now.
6. **Set the four undefined NFR targets** before QA2, so the hub load test can fail.
7. **Say `RA-Q09` out loud at the next client review**, as `[SEC]` itself asks.
